responsibility: This file provides the generic default implementations for a large portion of GCC’s target hook interface used by the middle end and backend when a port does not supply specialized behavior. It covers fallback logic for address legitimacy and legalization, calling convention details, libcall and builtin expansion hooks, varargs and EH defaults, mode promotion and compatibility, section/output policies, optimization cost and if-conversion heuristics, speculation-safety support, memory-tagging operations, gcov type sizing, and many other targetm entry points, often bridging older target macros to the newer hook-based interface.
same_name_distinction: Provides the actual generic default target hook implementations used by targetm, often bridging legacy target macros to the hook interface, whereas gcc/targhooks.h is the declaration catalog of those defaults for target hook initializers and overrides.
